metadata.technology_specification: Roller Compactor (also known as Roller Press)
metadata.technology_reasoning: Roller Compactors are widely used in industries such as pharmaceuticals, chemicals, and minerals for dry granulation by compressing powder between two rollers. The mechanical compression with counter-rotating rollers is the standard technology adopted for high throughput and consistent densification.

components.reasoning: Two counter-rotating rollers are the core mechanical compression elements, universally present, and form the primary functional component of the compactor.
The powder feeding subsystem ensures controlled and continuous delivery of material to the rollers, typically a separate assembly standardized in all designs.
Includes the electric motor and gearbox that drive the roller rotation, essential for operation and typically procured as separate units.
Mechanical or hydraulic system to control the gap between rollers, critical for adjusting compression force, always present as a distinct module.
Used to remove excess material from roller surfaces to prevent buildup, usually a component in most roller compactors as a separate subassembly or attachment.
Electronic control panel and sensors to regulate process parameters such as roller speed and force, standard in modern units as a separate system.
Conveys compacted ribbons or sheets away from rollers, usually a modular component distinct from the main compactor frame.
The structural assembly holding all components rigidly; a major part though usually manufactured or assembled in-house.

Roller Assembly.name: Steel Ingots
